day.note: Three votes are coming at me. I'll push back on Ellis, whose Hawk claim is duplicated and whose hug story doesn't add up, and call for a throw at Ellis.

day.text: Ellis is the Tit, that matches my list. Alex, you claim a Kookaburra visited Drew, but I only saw a Sphinx and a Tit. Either you're lying or you're the Sphinx. Alex, explain.

day.text: Blair's list is the only evidence against me, and Ellis only confirmed the Tit, not the Sphinx. If I visited Drew as Kookaburra, an honest Owl would have listed it. Blair either misread or lied. Drew, did anything odd show up in your visitor count? Let's not rush at Casey either.

day.text: Casey is the only one who admitted visiting me, and I was hugged, which only a Floofer does. Casey, the Hawk claim doesn't explain the hug. I'm leaning Casey as a cat, and I'd rather throw at Casey than wait.

Alex.confusing: How the Meowfia stake works: it only banks at 2x if you hit the eggsecuted Farm player, so it's unclear when throwing is worth it as a cat.
Alex.fun: Round 1, when the Owl, Eagle and Falcon reports lined up and we caught Blair's Hawk bluff.
Alex.change: Give the Meowfia a safer way to score, since staying hidden while the table votes for you left me with only 5 bonus points.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I hugged Blair and falsely claimed Hawk, which left three hugged visitors all pointing at me. I should have hugged someone else, or claimed a role consistent with being visited, and not pushed Finley, whose silence was pointing back at my partner.

Blair.confusing: The dawn reports and the hidden-role rules were hard to track, especially whether a Hawk visit can cause a hug and why an Owl's list didn't show every visitor. Night visits that landed on a Floofer also took a while to untangle.
Blair.fun: Round 2, when a Sphinx and a Tit visiting Drew came up and the table argued over whether Alex's Kookaburra claim was a lie. The table talk was tense and the reveals kept flipping.
Blair.change: I'd make the dawn reports name the visitor's animal when a hug happens, so hugs are easier to trace. I'd also show each player's own visit list to everyone at the start of the day so claims can be checked faster.
Blair.regret: In round 1 I claimed Hawk by copying Ellis's claim after being pressed, which made me look like the liar. Knowing I was Floofer, I'd have claimed a different Farm animal I could defend, or stayed quiet until I had a real reason to name a role.

Casey.confusing: How a Floofer's hug interacts with visits, such as whether a hugged Hawk's visit still counts and what visitors to a Floofer learn. It made some claims hard to check.
Casey.fun: Round 3, when Drew, Ellis and I all found we had visited Alex and been hugged. That pinned him as the Floofer and the table converged on him.
Casey.change: Give Meowfia a bit more to do at night, or a way to learn which claims are safe. A lone Floofer has little to bluff with once the table cross-checks visits.
Casey.regret: In round 2, as the Floofer, I admitted visiting Finley, who was a Turkey and ended up hugged. That tied me to the hug and got me eggsecuted. I should have claimed I visited someone else, or a role that didn't point at Finley.

Drew.confusing: The Sphinx and Floofer mechanics were hard to track from the dawn reports, and I never could tell whether a hug meant the hugger was a cat. The "stake banks" rules for Farm versus Meowfia throws were also easy to misread.
Drew.fun: Round 1 as the Sphinx: I learned the Owl was Alex and played it as a Farm-side accusation, then watched the table pile onto my own partner Blair. Casey's Floofer hug on Finley was a nice mess of conflicting claims.
Drew.change: I'd make the dawn reports name who visited whom, so visit claims can be checked directly instead of relying on people's word.
Drew.regret: In Round 1 I threw nothing and voted with the table on Blair, my own partner, which made me look like I was going along with the pile-on. I should have thrown at Ellis early to push the vote toward a Farm player and bank my stake.

Ellis.confusing: Nothing major, though how Floofer hugs interact with visitors' reports (the visitor gets hugged too) took a moment to work out.
Ellis.fun: Round 3, when the hug pattern on everyone who visited Alex exposed him as the Floofer, even after I got winked.
Ellis.change: Give Farm roles a bit more information, since many nights yielded nothing useful.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I stated my role and visit very openly and pushed hard on Alex early, which probably made me the Mouser's wink target. I would have shared the hug pattern but let others lead the accusation.

Finley.confusing: The final scores included "bonus" amounts that were never explained during play, and it wasn't clear how dead players' throws were scored. The Floofer's hug also made the visit-count clues hard to read.
Finley.fun: Round 2, when the table converged on Casey after Casey's Hawk story failed to explain the hug on the Turkey. Casey really was the Floofer, so the read was right.
Finley.change: Show each player's score pile breakdown and any bonus rules during the game, so players can judge who is ahead before the final reveal.
Finley.regret: In round 3, I winked Ellis, a Farm Eagle, on day one, which removed a key Farm voice early. Knowing Farm was pushing Alex, I should have stayed quiet and saved the Wink for a later Farm threat.
